The story uses sophisticated metaphor and personification to convey Judith’s estrangement and unease: the house seems capable of offering “resistance” and ultimately refuses to answer her listening. The faded-photograph comparison makes the familiar kitchen feel drained of life, while the sensation of the floor sinking gives physical form to her emotional disorientation. The fresh orange peels turn an ordinary domestic detail into an unsettling symbol of her mother’s lingering presence.
